analysis: Examined all supplied StandaloneServer.swift excerpts and the bounded patch against the canonical index and detailed T-041 definition. The changed load path removes the GLM pre-load digest comparison (base 1964–1971) and replaces post-load bracketing (base 2001–2004) with a claimed managed-load verified digest. This affects model identity (A-004, T-012, T-027) and SSD cache binding (T-041). Surrounding base code retains serialized memory admission, cancellation checks, pending-load accounting, cache eligibility decisions, native-owner checks and failure retirement. Head 1–587 supplies configuration, catalog filtering and lifecycle context but not the changed loading implementation. No concrete regression is established: removing redundant hashing can preserve identity if the managed loader verifies the exact bytes consumed and supplies an equivalent digest. The patch comment alone does not establish that contract, and the post-load replacement is truncated. Integration must inspect head 1964–2006, GLM5NextManagedLoad.adopting, ModelContainerLoading.loadServingContainer and manifest verification/digest derivation, confirming verification precedes serving, failures unwind ownership, and cacheEligibleWeightHash binds the actual loaded artifact. Compare aggregate digest semantics with the former hash and test substitution during loading. No supplied evidence changes bearer authentication, coordinator attestation, hop encryption, billing or privileged helper authority; their implementations were not examined here.
